_about: The one config of the local-model study. local_run.py, local_analyze.py and LOCAL_STUDY.md read every study value from here; the code holds none. Paths are relative to the repository root. Secrets never go here: the LM Studio token and the Honeycomb key are read from the environment variables named below (or .env.local, read-only).
question: Can local models drive mcp-for-kibana through a stated multi-step Kibana task, at which chain length do they lose track, and what does each step cost in time and tokens?

task.preamble: Using the kibana tools, work on Kibana's web-logs sample data (data view '{data_view}', index {logs_index}). Do these steps in order:
task.closing: Use only the kibana tools. When every step is done, reply with a short summary.

steps.text: Describe the data view '{data_view}': look up its fields and name its time field. End your reply with a line of the form TIME_FIELD: <field name>.
Build a dashboard titled '{marker} Web logs' on that data view with exactly two panels: the number of requests over time, and the number of requests by HTTP response code.

Create an alert rule named '{marker} 5xx errors' on the web-logs data for the signal of the response-code panel: it checks every minute and fires when more than 10 requests with a 5xx response code arrive within 5 minutes. The rule must be enabled when you finish: if it is created disabled, enable it.

Edit the response-code panel of that dashboard: change its title to 'Responses by code'. Then read the alert rule back and check that it is enabled. End your reply with a line of the form RULE_ENABLED: yes or RULE_ENABLED: no.
